newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina considering $2 bln bond - official.
newsitem.headline: Argentina considering $2 bln bond - official.

text.p: Argentina will decide in January whether to accept an offer to place a $2 billion bond in dollars, Finance Under-Secretary Miguel Kiguel said Monday.
"We have received that big offer but we have also received other, smaller offers," Kiguel told a news conference.
"We'll have to decide in January. If we see the market is in good shape and we consider that it is the right moment we are going to come out with that sort of bond," he said.
The $250-million Letes treasury bill placement due Tuesday will be Argentina's last issue this year.
Kiguel said "the most likely thing" is the first placement in 1997 will be in dollars.

"For 1997 we are already looking at offers in several currencies and looking at the dollar, the yen and the mark. But we have just made placements in marks and yens so the most likely thing is that our next issue will be in dollars," he said.
Argentina could also make peso placements in 1997, "for small amounts around 250 million", Kiguel said.
